data.text:
Sanjay Singh vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Deptt. ... on 22 
May, 2024 
Author: Abdul Moin
Bench: Abdul Moin
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad, Lucknow Bench
?Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc-Lko:38739
Court No. - 6
Case :- Writ - A No. - 3950 of 2024
Petitioner :- Sanjay Singh 
Respondent :- State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Deptt. Food Safety Drug Administration, Lk
Counsel for Petitioner :- Mahendra Pratap Singh,Ranjit Singh 
Counsel for Respondent :- C.S.C.
Hon'ble Abdul Moin,J.
1. Heard.
2.  Admittedly, against the order of punishment dated 09.04.2023, the petitioner has a statutory remedy of filing of an appeal before the appellate authority. 
3. Learned counsel for the petitioner contends that as it is the Head of Department i.e. the Commissioner, who has passed the order impugned consequently no appeal would lie as the order itself has been passed by the appellate authority. 
Sanjay Singh vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Deptt. ... on 22 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/11915094/
1 4. The aforesaid argument is patently fallacious inasmuch as it is settled provision of law that an appeal would lie to a still higher authority than the authority who has passed the order impugned. 
5. Considering the aforesaid, the writ petition is disposed of leaving it open to the petitioner to file an appeal against the impugned order. It is provided that in case an appeal is filed within a period of two weeks from today along with certified copy of this order then the appellate authority shall proceed to consider and decide the same on merits in accordance with law within a period of six weeks from the date of filing of the appeal.
Order Date :- 22.5.2024 A. Katiyar  Sanjay Singh vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Deptt. ... on 22 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/11915094/
